In line with the timeline outlined in the “Action Plan” for accelerating progress toward net-zero targets, we will gradually integrate environmental and social considerations into our strategies, risk assessments, and reporting processes at a practical pace, further advancing our corporate sustainability efforts. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a dual materiality assessment to gain deeper insights into the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on matters of greatest significance. Additionally, we will carry out energy audits and utilize technological solutions to evaluate the significant impact of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby strengthening our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We fully support the Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap issued by the government and are actively preparing to comply with ISSB standards for disclosure. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to honor its commitment to energy efficiency and conservation by selecting data centers for planned upgrades based on these principles. We will also expand digital initiatives aimed at promoting sustainability and efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to facilitate paperless processes and waste reduction, as well as enhancing the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the general public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Leveraging its multiple roles as a central bank, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainability advocate, the HKMA plays a part in promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust governance framework for sustainability that guides the development of relevant strategies and policies, oversees implementation efforts, and ensures that sustainability considerations are integrated into its own operations. Committed to sound corporate governance, the HKMA has put in place a well-structured governance framework for sustainability featuring clear accountability mechanisms and high transparency. This framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively incorporated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, while also providing effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate progress and outcomes in sustainability initiatives. The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises the following components:   – The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant subcommittees, which oversee the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability efforts, and provide recommendations;   – The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which provides leadership at the management level regarding the HKMA’s overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategies and policies;   – In the realm of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and oversees all ESG-related activities within the Office; and   – For other functional areas, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures related to banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) jointly established the Inter-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (the Steering Group) to coordinate efforts among financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other parties, thereby accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the HKMA’s sustainability initiatives over recent years, the Steering Committee was established in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and better coordinate all sustainability efforts across the HKMA’s various functional areas. Its responsibilities include:   – Providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans related to ESG matters in four key areas: banking, development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations;   – Overseeing implementation of ESG-related plans by various HKMA departments;   – Evaluating the HKMA’s performance and achievements in attaining its ESG objectives; and   – Supervising external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. Additionally, Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development are invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on major achievements and future plans. The Steering Committee meets regularly, with support provided by relevant working groups under the Banking Department, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Relations Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Apart from developing and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC jointly launched the Steering Group in May 2020. Acting as a cross-institutional platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts within the financial industry to address climate and environmental risks, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For further details on the Steering Group’s work, please refer to the chapter “Strengthening the Development of a Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem.”

Climate change poses risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been working to strengthen the Hong Kong financial system’s resilience to climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are exposed to various sustainability- and climate-related issues in their day-to-day operations; therefore, they must proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play a vital role in the financial system by channeling funds toward green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places special emphasis on building banks’ capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, as well as accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA launched the “Sustainable Finance Action Plan” (the “Action Plan”), which outlines its vision to further cement Hong Kong’s position as a regional sustainable finance hub and to support sustainable development in Asia and beyond. The Action Plan comprises eight objectives across four key areas. To help the industry achieve these objectives under relevant banking policies, we have been undertaking the following initiatives: All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 and net-zero emissions in their financing activities by 2050; all banks will enhance transparency regarding climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared best practices on transition planning with the industry and launched a consultation on a draft version of Section GS-2 “Transition Planning” in the Supervisory Policy Manual. This new section aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks’ capabilities to cope with the net-zero transition and on managing related risks. Additionally, we are reviewing the regulatory review process used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy levels and determine their Pillar capital requirements. The purpose of this review is to incorporate relevant factors identified by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, thereby encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks—including transition planning—to address climate risks. The HKMA has been striving to align local sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board’s Sustainability Reporting Standards (ISSB Standards) and the Basel Committee’s disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is currently analyzing recent developments in sustainable disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a feasibility study on adopting the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Plan. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (the “Taxonomy”) to address industry concerns over greenwashing and to help channel funds toward green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors; it is designed to be aligned with the Common Green Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while also incorporating elements tailored to local conditions. We have now commenced the next phase of the work to expand the scope of the Taxonomy, and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable financing. Throughout the year, the HKMA further tightened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and remained committed to helping banks build the capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to respond to climate change. The HKMA also completed all tasks under its two-year plan formulated in 2022 aimed at integrating climate risks into banking regulatory processes. To enhance banks’ ability to manage climate risks, the HKMA shares best practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings with the banking sector. These include:   – Establishing a robust governance framework that clearly defines the responsibilities of the Board of Directors and senior management;   – Ensuring effective monitoring of key aspects related to climate risks: (1) facilitating and overseeing the formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) applying appropriate oversight to climate risk management; and (3) fostering a strong climate risk culture within the organization. In August, the HKMA also held a Balanced Supervision Roundtable focusing on climate risk management. In August, the HKMA hosted a balanced regulatory roundtable focused on climate risk management. At the event, bank representatives and HKMA officials exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, such as challenges banks face in managing climate risks, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance. This roundtable served as an interactive platform for information sharing and aided the HKMA in its regulatory efforts concerning climate risks. The HKMA conducted a thematic review of banks’ climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against regulatory expectations outlined in Module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management” of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The review covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control, mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. A second series of consultation meetings was held to evaluate progress made by a new batch of banks in implementing Module GS-1, as well as to understand the challenges they encounter. These meetings also addressed recent regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, such as transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing. Tailored feedback and guidance were provided to banks based on their specific circumstances to support their climate risk management efforts. In 2024, the HKMA completed the second round of the Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST), with participation from 21 retail banks and Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. Results indicated that under various scenarios—including those where climate risks coincide with macroeconomic downturns—the Hong Kong banking sector continues to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared to the pilot phase of CRST, participating banks significantly improved their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report detailing CRST findings and best practices observed by the HKMA was published in February 2025. Recognizing the numerous challenges banks face regarding data and methodologies in climate risk management, the HKMA has been actively promoting the application of technology to address these issues. To tackle the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to evaluate potential impacts of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Moving forward, the platform will be enhanced based on user feedback and by incorporating additional local data. Furthermore, the HKMA collaborates with relevant stakeholders to encourage adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services industry. This year, we released implementation guidelines and two briefing notes on RegTech use cases (in English) outlining technological solutions for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) assessments, sustainability management, and mitigating greenwashing risks. We also hosted the third “FiNETech” event, bringing together over 150 financial institutions and tech firms to discuss collaboration in green fintech. Fully aware of the potential risks climate change poses to the financial system, the HKMA incorporates a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research, thereby strengthening its ongoing monitoring efforts. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the HKMA takes climate change into account and incorporates analyses of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. By actively participating in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps to further enrich climate scenarios, thereby assisting central banks and regulators in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS released the fifth version of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, which serve as a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA contributes to analyzing the interplay between transition planning by financial and non-financial firms and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA has published a “Guidelines on Banks’ Application of Green Technologies” (English version), providing financial institutions with best practices for utilizing green technologies to facilitate their transition to net zero. In terms of research, the HKMA has undertaken multiple applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change on the financial sector and the broader economy. Research topics include the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in mitigating the effects of monetary policy shocks, the influence of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in the transition to a low-carbon economy. These research findings not only deepen our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also offer valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, aiding policy formulation. Locally, these studies help the HKMA continuously monitor and assess the impact of climate change on financial stability. The results are also shared with a wide range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels, including the HKMA Research Memoranda. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary Research (HKIMR), the research arm of the Institute of Financial Studies, has published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission firms can reap substantial benefits from carbon pricing, highlighting its role in improving efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. This research is featured in the HKIMR’s “Insights from Monetary Research” and is shared with local and international scholars and policy researchers. The HKMA’s “Liquidity Arrangement Framework” is a collateralized standby funding facility designed to provide timely liquidity support to banks in need. Under this framework, the HKMA now incorporates sustainability considerations when evaluating eligible collateral. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions aimed at addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such engagement, we help foster policy dialogue on climate change and its implications for financial stability at both international and regional levels, while drawing valuable lessons to strengthen Hong Kong’s financial system’s resilience to climate-related challenges.

To strengthen Hong Kong’s position as a leading regional hub for green and sustainable finance, the HKMA is committed to raising market awareness and participation, providing necessary infrastructure and incentives, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As outlined in the HKMA’s “Sustainable Finance Action Plan,” the HKMA strives to enhance the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we aim to position Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers both regionally and globally, support technological innovation in the green financial sector, improve sustainable disclosure practices within the industry, expand the local pool of green talent, and address knowledge gaps related to sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Positioning Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform regionally and globally; fostering innovation in sustainable finance; promoting high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure; and bridging talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance within the region. To demonstrate the government’s commitment to tackling climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the “Government Green Bond Programme” was launched in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the government in issuing green bonds worth approximately USD 280 billion in total, which were sold to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, including green building, waste management and recycling, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. With each issuance, we continue to innovate and expand the features of green bonds—including currency options, tenors, and distribution channels—thereby setting a precedent for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to amplify the programme’s impact and further consolidate Hong Kong’s status as a green and sustainable finance hub, its scope was broadened to include sustainable projects and it was renamed the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme.”  To enhance transparency and accountability under the Sustainable Bond Programme, the government publishes an annual “Green Bond Report” detailing how funds raised through green bonds are allocated and their anticipated environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the government in issuing institutional green bonds worth approximately USD 30 billion under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This multi-currency issuance featured bonds denominated in RMB, USD, and EUR with varying tenors. The bonds attracted participation from diverse investor groups, receiving strong demand with total subscriptions exceeding USD 150 billion. Notably, the 20-year and 30-year RMB green bonds marked the government’s first-ever issuances of such tenors, establishing new benchmarks in the market and further underscoring the exemplary role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also enriched the range of offshore RMB investment products available in Hong Kong. Moreover, the enthusiastic response from global investors reflects their confidence in Hong Kong’s efforts to advance green and sustainable development. To encourage more regional borrowers to leverage Hong Kong’s financing platform for sustainable development funding, the HKMA continues to administer the “Green and Sustainable Finance Subsidy Scheme” introduced in May 2021, which provides subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The scheme has been well received by the industry; as of end-2024, it has approved subsidies for some 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, totaling over USD 1,400 billion. In May 2024, the scheme was extended for three more years until 2027, with its scope expanded to include transition bonds and loans. This extension and expansion aim to motivate borrowers in relevant industries across the region to utilize Hong Kong’s transition financing platform for gradual decarbonization. – Subsidies approved for some 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, totaling over USD 1,400 billion (as of end-2024);   – Scheme extended to 2027 with expanded coverage to transition financing instruments. Meanwhile, the HKMA has been actively promoting Hong Kong’s sustainable financing platform, achieving commendable results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government conducted its fourth offshore issuance of local government bonds in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 70 billion, which included RMB 27 billion in green bonds, RMB 10 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB 9 billion in social responsibility bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial People’s Government made its debut offshore bond issuance in Hong Kong, raising RMB 50 billion, of which RMB 15 billion comprised green bonds. In October, the People’s Government of Hainan Province conducted its third offshore bond issuance in Hong Kong, raising RMB 30 billion in total. This comprised RMB 10 billion in blue bonds and RMB 10 billion in sustainable bonds. These bond issuances once again highlight Hong Kong’s unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable financing between the Chinese mainland and the rest of the world. Thanks to these efforts, Hong Kong continues to solidify its standing as the preferred platform for sustainable finance in Asia. According to statistics released by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong remained the largest hub in Asia for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances in 2024, with a total volume of USD 431 billion arranged through Hong Kong, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To spur innovation in sustainable finance, the HKMA assisted the government in issuing two landmark tokenized green bonds in 2023 and 2024—the world’s first tokenized government green bonds and the first multi-currency digital bonds, respectively. These issuances reflect the government’s support for market participants in applying asset tokenization and innovative technologies to green and sustainable finance. In November, the HKMA launched the “Digital Bond Subsidy Scheme” to encourage and support innovation within Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance markets by promoting the issuance of digital bonds, including digital green bonds. A working group on sustainable disclosure under the Inter-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance has been working to facilitate Hong Kong’s adoption of the International Sustainability Standards Board’s (ISSB) standards. In December 2024, the government released the “Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap,” outlining a clear pathway for large listed companies to fully adopt ISSB standards by 2028 at the latest. The HKMA has been collaborating closely with local and international partners to help entities at various stages of readiness achieve high-quality sustainable disclosure, thereby making such practices more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the use of the “Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-Listed Companies,” jointly developed by the Steering Group and CDP in 2022. This questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template, facilitating sustainable disclosure efforts by enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the questionnaire was launched in February 2024, allowing companies to submit responses online (see the QR code below). Based on industry feedback and recent international developments, the HKMA is refining the questionnaire to make it even more user-friendly; measures include identifying core questions and providing common use cases. We are also striving to improve its compatibility with other tools available on the Steering Group’s website. For further information on the questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The HKMA itself adheres to the latest global standards by providing high-quality sustainable disclosures in its “Sustainability Report,” thereby demonstrating its own commitment to sustainability. The report contains detailed information on climate-related operational risks faced by the HKMA, as well as its plans and progress toward achieving climate-related objectives. For specifics on the HKMA’s own sustainability disclosures, please refer to the “HKMA and Sustainability” section. Given the rapidly evolving nature of the sustainable finance landscape, the HKMA is intensifying efforts to build skills within the banking sector and promote knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders, aiming to bridge existing knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance local bankers’ understanding and capabilities in sustainable finance, the HKMA, in collaboration with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers, launched the foundational level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the “Banking Professional Qualifications Framework” in July 2023. This module aims to help banking professionals acquire relevant knowledge and develop competencies in green and sustainable finance more effectively, covering four main areas: (1) green and sustainable financial products and services; (2) sustainable/climate risk management; (3) sustainable disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainable strategies, compliance, and governance. Additionally, the professional level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, targeted at mid- to senior-level bankers, was launched in November. To provide necessary training for banking professionals, the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers, as the administrator of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, introduced foundational-level training courses in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking sector in 2025 to develop a professional-level training course. To better understand the banking industry’s evolving skill and training needs, the HKMA is currently partnering with industry stakeholders on a study titled “Future Banking Talent 2026–2030,” with findings scheduled for release in 2025. This joint research effort serves as a follow-up to the “Future Banking Talent 2021–2025” report published in June 2020. The outcomes of this follow-up study will provide valuable guidance for the industry in formulating and adjusting talent development strategies and measures, thereby supporting the sustainable growth of the banking sector. Through collaboration with the Steering Group, the HKMA also continues to facilitate the implementation of the government-funded “Pilot Scheme on Green and Sustainable Finance Training,” which subsidizes training related to sustainable finance for industry practitioners, graduates, and students. As of December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses have been registered as eligible training programs under this scheme, with over 5,700 reimbursement applications approved. In its “Budget 2025–26,” the government announced that this scheme will be extended through 2028. Leveraging its expertise, the HKMA actively promotes skills development and knowledge exchange through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the Capacity Building for Sustainable Investment Alliance (CASI), the HKMA’s Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop in Hong Kong in June, focusing on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks, and innovative financial tools. Furthermore, the HKMA supported the establishment of a Hong Kong chapter of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in October, and will utilize GFANZ’s network and expertise to further strengthen skills development in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Leveraging its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can go hand in hand, the HKMA adheres to responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund. It gives priority to sustainable assets and requires its external investment managers to actively exercise their ownership rights. Guided by the principle of “preserving capital while seeking long-term appreciation,” the HKMA invests prudently, believing that due consideration of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate investment risks and unlocks the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place special emphasis on sustainability, particularly the urgent issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieve better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We incorporate ESG factors in a practical and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment tools to channel capital toward sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA released its “HKMA ESG Expectations” and made the document available to its investment partners via its annual ESG workshop and website. We collaborate with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to establish industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment practices within the financial sector and central banking community. Through these joint efforts, we strive to foster a future where finance and sustainable development progress hand in hand. In October, the HKMA unveiled its “Sustainable Finance Action Plan” (the “Action Plan”), which further reinforces its commitment to investing in a sustainable future by aiming to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 through the Exchange Fund’s portfolio and by mobilizing partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the framework and guiding principles for responsible investment, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the management of the Fund’s investments. The primary guiding principle establishes the overall tone for how the HKMA can balance responsible investment practices with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, oversees ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund’s investments. It reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policies, and monitors their implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team within the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, coordinates and oversees all ESG-related activities within the Office. Proposals and progress updates discussed at its quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and comprising the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office and the Chief Strategy Officer, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across various HKMA functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to achieve the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Unit collaborates closely with various teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office in integrating ESG factors. It also assists senior management of the Office in managing ESG-related risks and opportunities—particularly those related to climate—across all investment portfolios:  - Public market investments: The Credit, Regulation and Oversight Committee, composed of senior officials from the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews how ESG factors are incorporated into credit risk models based on input from the Sustainable Investment Unit. Meanwhile, the Risk Management and Oversight Department regularly monitors the ESG performance of the fixed-income portfolio. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Unit contributes from an ESG perspective to the selection, appointment, and oversight of external fund managers managing the equity portfolio (for details, see the section “Promoting active ownership” under “Risk Management” on page 39).  - Private market investments: The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments provided by both the private market investment and risk management teams for each proposed investment. The HKMA recognizes that physical and transition risks associated with climate change, as well as related opportunities, can affect the long-term financial performance of Exchange Fund investments. According to the United Nations Environment Programme’s “Emissions Gap Report 2024,” global average temperatures are projected to rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels unless there is a substantial global effort to rapidly cut greenhouse gas emissions. Uncertainties surrounding policy changes, technological developments, and shifts in behavior in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and impacting asset valuations. At the same time, the growing frequency and severity of extreme weather events pose additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investments. Amid these challenges, governments and industries worldwide are increasingly turning to sustainable solutions, creating potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon technologies, emerging innovations, and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives; therefore, it places special emphasis on climate-related considerations when integrating ESG factors. The HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, and it is pursuing this goal through a structured three-pronged approach (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA released an “Action Plan” outlining its commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA favors proactive engagement rather than exclusion or divestment from investable assets.  Investing in a sustainable future: - The Exchange Fund portfolio aims to reach net-zero emissions by 2050. - Actively expand the scope and variety of sustainable investments, particularly those focused on climate transition in both public and private markets. - Integrate ESG factors—with special attention to climate change and transition prospects—into every investment decision. - Establish clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, requiring all external fund managers, investee companies, and counterparties to comply. - Strive to reduce the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund’s equity portfolio by 67% from its 2017 level by 2030.  Supporting regional transition through investment: - Continue engaging with external fund managers to identify and optimize investment opportunities that drive transition efforts. - Keep seeking and prioritizing high-quality investment opportunities that facilitate Asia’s transition while delivering positive global impacts.  First, maintaining a diversified and robust portfolio is essential to achieving the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. Excluding certain sectors or industries outright would narrow the pool of investable assets, potentially affecting both investment returns and risk profiles. Through a compatible approach, the HKMA is able to seize opportunities to invest in enterprises undergoing transformation—including those in high-emission industries—that possess advanced technologies and sound corporate governance to adapt to evolving global climate trends. Secondly, addressing climate change necessitates the transformation of core “brown” industries. Merely excluding or divesting from relevant investments will not help resolve the issue of carbon emissions. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising its asset ownership rights, the HKMA supports these industries in transitioning to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about beneficial changes both for itself and globally. The HKMA’s net-zero investment policy has evolved from a preference for green or low-carbon assets to also encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, thereby driving overall decarbonization of the economy. As a global asset owner, the HKMA recognizes that the long-term resilience of its portfolio depends not only on its own adjustments but also on broader economic transformation. Although there is no perfect single solution, in 2024 the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategy by adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to foster such transformation while supporting both the Exchange Fund and global net-zero objectives. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, tilting the portfolio toward decarbonization, and making thematic investments in various asset classes aligned with pathways toward net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio toward ESG-leading firms or companies providing climate solutions, coupled with stewardship efforts to drive corporate transformation. In private markets, greater emphasis is placed on investments that facilitate such transition. By incorporating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify opportunities that promote climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes now account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund’s overall portfolio, with financial performance comparable to relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5).  – Public Market Investments: The HKMA has developed an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and has extended the use of customized low-carbon equity indices to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social, and sustainability (GSS) bonds that offer competitive returns while financing sustainable projects (see the section “Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds” for relevant case studies).  – Private Market Investments: The HKMA strives to build a robust long-term growth portfolio by capitalizing on investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, it actively identifies and evaluates opportunities that can accelerate energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with multinational organizations (examples are provided in the section “Collaborating to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond”). - Passive investment portfolios that use ESG indices as investment benchmarks   - Customized decarbonization strategies for passive and active quantitative investment portfolios whose benchmarks are non-ESG indices   - Active investment portfolios focused on governance themes   - Active ESG investment portfolios centered on sustainability and climate transition   - Sustainable projects such as renewable energy infrastructure, as well as green-certified buildings and warehouses   - Funds dedicated to energy transition and decarbonization efforts globally, in Asia, and in the Global South   - Green, social responsibility, and sustainability bonds   - A green bond fund managed by an international organization   - The “Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program” (MCPP) administered by the International Finance Corporation, which focuses on financing sustainable projects in emerging markets   - The “MCPP One Planet” initiative, which provides climate-related investments in emerging markets aligned with the Paris Agreement    The Authority has invested in green bonds issued by a quasi-governmental entity. The funds raised through these green bonds are allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading outdated equipment at various wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades involve optimizing monitoring and control systems as well as pump performance, thereby generating positive environmental benefits in wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to continuously treating wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertilizer, charcoal, cement, and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recycling rate of up to 100%. The facilities also utilize gases generated during sludge treatment to fuel boilers and generate electricity.    The Authority has also invested in green bonds issued by a multilateral development bank. These bonds finance numerous projects, including the restoration of a national canal system. As one of the country’s largest irrigation systems, the canals are designed to channel excess river water to arid regions. The primary objective of this project is to repair deteriorating canal linings to prevent leaks, conserve water, improve water-use efficiency, and reclaim waterlogged land. Additionally, the project provides skill training for local stakeholders, promoting the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation techniques such as micro-irrigation, as well as sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organization. In 2024, one of its key priorities in fulfilling this commitment is to advance its target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its operations to 2030—20 years earlier than originally planned—in line with the Sustainable Finance Action Plan. Beyond promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to employee training, physical and mental well-being, financial inclusion, and enhancing public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, serves as the main decision-making body for all corporate sustainability initiatives. Demonstrating its dedication to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions in its operations by 2030, as part of the Sustainable Finance Action Plan. At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Institutional Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainability measures related to operations, employee well-being, and social engagement, and regularly reports to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division acts as the central coordinator and hub for implementing, communicating, and reporting on corporate sustainability efforts. Complementary support is also provided by the Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Group, both composed of staff from various operational departments; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming ideas on creating a greener workplace, while the latter aims to foster a culture of volunteerism among employees. In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to environmental protection, employees, and society at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the “15 Years and Above Caring Partnership” badge for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA’s sustainability strategy continues to be structured around three pillars: environmental responsibility, employee welfare, and social responsibility.   - Focus on carbon reduction and digitalization in daily operations, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030.   - Adopt green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines.   - Promote more environmentally friendly practices within the financial industry and broader society.   - Cultivate a motivated workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA’s strategic objectives.   - Foster a collaborative, caring, and inclusive work environment that values diversity and strengthens employee engagement.   - Provide a high-quality workplace conducive to healthy lifestyles.   - Nurture a culture of social responsibility.   - Integrate social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management.   - Promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy through consumer education initiatives.    The HKMA takes climate change seriously and leads by example. In October 2024, it announced plans to advance its target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its operations to 2030—20 years earlier than previously committed—as part of the Sustainable Finance Action Plan. The HKMA has revised its roadmap toward net-zero transition, emphasizing responsible management of its environmental impact through carbon reduction, energy conservation, paper minimization, and waste recycling, while fully leveraging improvements in the local power company’s fuel mix. Additionally, the HKMA has developed a digital work environment to boost efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. Recognizing the importance of cultivating a sustainability-oriented culture, the HKMA continuously runs promotional programs and activities to encourage employees to adopt sustainable practices. Under its overarching 2030 net-zero target, the HKMA is actively exploring the use of carbon-embedded tools across its value chain to further cut emissions and ensure low-carbon procurement wherever possible. Since 2023, it has fully offset carbon emissions from business travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset programs. Moving forward, the HKMA intends to expand these carbon-embedded and carbon-offset initiatives to cover all remaining major sources of emissions. In addition to the aforementioned environmental commitments related to its day-to-day operations, the HKMA continues to promote the market’s low-carbon transition, ranging from introducing electronic document submission and processing procedures to encouraging electronic payments and facilitating the return of coins into circulation. The remainder of this chapter elaborates on the HKMA’s strategies in promoting environmental protection, as well as fostering employees’ physical and mental well-being and demonstrating social responsibility. Under the HKMA’s overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee chaired by the Chief Executive oversees and reviews potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its operations, including those arising from climate change. To better assess the possible impacts of climate change on its operations, the HKMA identifies various climate-related risks and examines their actual and potential effects. To address these risks while ensuring business continuity, the HKMA’s offices incorporate multiple measures aimed at mitigating potential physical hazards, fires, and other emergencies. Additionally, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans to include comprehensive measures covering not only its offices but also its communications and IT infrastructure. Evacuation drills and exercises to activate backup facilities are conducted periodically to ensure staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA also continuously monitors its transition risks by tracking greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage resulting from its operations. Its latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 related to its operations by 2030 at the latest. These targets were established with reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative. The HKMA utilizes the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its emissions. Scope 1 emissions consist of direct emissions from petrol-powered vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA’s primary greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect emissions resulting from electricity generated by burning fossil fuels. In the absence of data from individual suppliers, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimating major Scope 3 emissions stemming from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills, as well as employees’ air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are presented in the “Performance Summary” on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency; the scope and baseline of this verification are outlined in the “Verification Statement” appended at the end of this report. The HKMA practices what it preaches, adhering to the same climate-related standards expected of banks under its supervision and the broader financial system. As a first step toward greener mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric ones in 2024, and will continue this effort in 2025 to achieve fully eco-friendly transportation. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, during various renovation projects in 2024, it reused existing furniture and building materials or offered trade-in discounts on new items to minimize waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and conservation measures in its offices and data centers. In 2024, it incorporated a modularly designed uninterruptible power supply system into its data center upgrades, further improving the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data center. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improved operational efficiency under partial load, and integration of advanced cooling technologies and higher power density, all of which help reduce overall energy consumption. Through its digital workplace initiatives, the HKMA also strengthens virtual collaboration internally, streamlining workflows and effectively reducing paper usage. Additionally, taking into account manufacturers’ software update cycles, the HKMA has extended the service life of its mobile and desktop devices, thereby prolonging their secure usage period. To minimize office waste, the HKMA adheres to the “4R” principles—refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle—and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Recycling bins for various materials are placed at multiple convenient locations throughout the office. To further improve recycling rates, the HKMA introduced dedicated recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit net bags in 2024. Since November 2022, food waste collected at the HKMA has been sent to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department’s “Waste Reduction Commitment” initiative, pledging to adopt measures aimed at reducing waste generated from its various activities. The HKMA continues to prioritize the procurement of goods meeting the environmental specifications outlined in the Government’s “Green Procurement List,” particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To curb carbon emissions from business travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their trips carefully, such as combining multiple overseas trips whenever possible. At the institutional level, since 2023 the HKMA has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel, resulting in a reduction of approximately 10% in annual carbon emissions from air travel. Furthermore, the HKMA participates in the “Gold Standard” certified carbon offset program to offset any remaining emissions; this program focuses on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA organized various learning activities for staff, including talks and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on April 22, 2024, through the entire month of May, the HKMA held its first “HKMA Green Month” under the theme “Green Thinking, Green Living, Green Working.” This served as an excellent opportunity for the HKMA to demonstrate its commitment and motivation toward integrating environmental sustainability into its internal operations. Activities included a “Sustainability BINGO Scorecard” encouraging staff to adopt greener habits, a “Save the Earth” quiz, and a workshop on caring for “moss balls,” an indoor plant cultivation technique originating from Japan. Additionally, waste audit results were shared, and representatives from a community recycling center provided guidance on best recycling practices. To sustain the momentum generated by the Green Month, the HKMA launched a six-month recycling campaign in October, emphasizing responsible waste management and underscoring how small individual behavioral changes can significantly improve the organization’s overall recycling performance. A highlight of this campaign was the release of a video series titled “Green ‘Fit’ Actions,” in which senior executives shared practical recycling tips. The campaign also featured a range of screen savers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and electronic reminders encouraging staff to reduce waste and increase recycling efforts. At year-end 2024, the HKMA conducted an employee questionnaire survey to gauge staff awareness of sustainability issues and to gather their opinions on proposed green office measures. The findings will inform future sustainability training programs and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong’s central banking institution, the HKMA regards itself as a key agent of change; it is thus committed to accelerating the low-carbon transition and promoting sustainable practices within the financial sector and broader society. The HKMA has implemented multiple measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the “Shared Data Submission Platform” in 2023, the HKMA expanded its services in 2024 to include non-bank entities such as operators of stored-value payment instruments, thereby facilitating their submission of certain regulatory data. The expansion of the platform’s services aims to further streamline the submission process for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA’s commitment to sustainable development. Other new initiatives launched in 2024 include SurveyTool, which enables banks to respond to HKMA questionnaires through a simplified submission process, and an intelligent information and document management system that offers users a centralized platform with advanced search capabilities for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (“Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (“HKMA”). The Data includes total energy consumption in 2024, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper usage, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills), greenhouse gas emissions from air travel, as well as their respective intensity values. Additionally, the Data covers Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions arising from purchases of goods and services, capital goods, fuel and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills), and employee commuting in both 2023 and 2024, together with their corresponding intensity values. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emission data was compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”) jointly issued by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covered a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, of which 5 offices are located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and the warehouse is at 6) Lok Sing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the Data, as well as to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative samples of data and supporting evidence from the 6 assets. This verification was carried out in compliance with the “International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised)” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board, specifically the provisions pertaining to “Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information.” The verification procedures were designed to enable the formation of an opinion and to provide a reasonable level of assurance. These procedures adhered to the requirements set forth in the GHG Protocol. To assess data integrity and accuracy, the verification process entailed tracing selected sample data back to their sources; it also involved reviewing the basic procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, followed by reliability testing. Furthermore, the internal data collection and management mechanisms were evaluated through interviews with personnel responsible for data preparation, and representative data and documentation were examined. All relevant raw data and supporting evidence were thoroughly reviewed during the verification process. The HKMA bears responsibility for data collection and reporting. Our verification work was conducted in complete independence and impartiality; the verification team at the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency had no involvement whatsoever in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency can reasonably assure that:   – The Data is substantially accurate and reliable;   – The HKMA’s overall data collection mechanisms are adequate.
